requirement_or_question: Because manifest records follow data, sequential extraction stages decoded content and creates no destination object until framing, every Chunk digest, EAM invariants, identity roots, footer binding and exact length are established; a corrupt final Chunk leaves no destination, existing objects are never replaced (EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION), and materialization reads plaintext only through verified sources.

requirement_or_question: Since Entry records follow all Chunk data and frames are digest-ordered, a sequential extractor cannot materialize any file before EOF and must stage the whole archive plaintext (temporary disk roughly equal to extracted size, total_bytes may refuse large archives); tar-like incremental extraction and early output are structurally impossible in stream-layout-v1.

requirement_or_question: Sequential staging keeps a resident plaintext set up to StagingLimits.memory_bytes and spills the rest (FIFO, oversize items direct) to a private create_new temporary file bounded by total_bytes; memory_only(n) forbids spill; archive plaintext is never required in RAM; staging is released on success, failure and truncation; peak resident, spilled bytes and retained Chunks are reported; staging I/O errors are PolicyRefused/Io, never Corrupt.

requirement_or_question: StagingLimits.total_bytes is cumulative: staged_bytes is never decremented on release and released spill space is not reclaimed until drop, so the limit bounds bytes ever staged per pass (default 64 GiB), not concurrent usage.

requirement_or_question: Spilled plaintext is written unencrypted to std::env::temp_dir() with default OS permissions and a pid/counter/nanosecond name; deletion happens only in Drop so a crash leaves decoded plaintext on disk; the staging directory is not configurable (64 name attempts then PolicyRefused/Io).

requirement_or_question: Any error reading the Index section, including a caller-policy refusal (e.g. Index larger than 64 MiB), is silently mapped to RebuiltInvalid and triggers a full header scan; conversely Index validation checks only that locators lie within CHUNK_DATA and are unique, so a Chunk missing from an otherwise valid Index fails EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_DEPENDENCY_INVALID without falling back to a scan.

requirement_or_question: Reading a dependent Chunk decodes up to max_lookback preceding group members for a 1 MiB reference prefix, and the reader computes the lookback closure before prefetch (refused above max_dependency_chunks); but each predecessor is itself prefix-coded and decoded recursively, so reading a late member transitively decodes the whole preceding run (up to 128 Chunks), while inspection and explain report max_lookback and one-level closures.

requirement_or_question: Only the final 1 MiB of concatenated preceding plaintext is used as reference prefix, yet up to 8 preceding Chunks (possibly multi-MiB) must be decoded; the efficiency of lookback 4/8 with large Chunks is unanalysed.

requirement_or_question: RandomReadSource is a public Send+Sync trait (len, read_exact_at, revision) with SourceRevision Memory{length, sha256}, Local{length, modified_nanos} or Http{length, strong_etag}; backends exist for immutable memory (hashed at construction), one held local file handle (Mutex-serialized seek+read, no pread) and HTTP(S); custom sources are allowed; RangeSession bounds-checks every offset/extent before allocation, enforces per-range, request, byte and metadata budgets before fetching, and is pub(crate).

requirement_or_question: A random-access session pins the source revision observed at open (refusing a length disagreement with EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE), bounds all reads by the pinned length, and rechecks detectable revision state before returning metadata or content: open and each read_entry end with a fresh revision fetch (an extra HEAD over HTTP) whose mismatch fails the operation.
research_needed: Measure the latency/request cost of per-operation HEAD revalidation over high-RTT links; ETag change mid-session in integration tests.

requirement_or_question: A strong ETag pins only the server-declared revision; archive integrity mechanisms authenticate fetched bytes, so a server mixing revisions or altering bytes under one ETag should cause detection, not wrong output.
research_needed: Adversarial range server serving mixed revisions, altered frames, altered Index/Manifest under a stable ETag; confirm every case yields a typed failure.

requirement_or_question: Revision rechecks cover only detectable state; a held local file revision is length plus modified_nanos, so in-place same-length writes within mtime granularity, truncation races and platform share-mode differences may go undetected mid-session (digests should still prevent wrong output).
research_needed: Platform tests (Windows share modes, POSIX in-place writes, network filesystems) of what local revision detection catches; confirm digest verification still prevents wrong output.
decision_needed: What revision signal (size, mtime, file ID, locks) must local sources use, and what guarantee is documented when change is undetectable?

requirement_or_question: The session cache is revision-scoped, bounded by caller-owned max_cached_bytes (default 128 MiB), and uses deterministic FIFO eviction; a read is served only when fully contained in one cached entry, entries larger than the bound are not cached, and ranges spanning adjacent cached entries are refetched.
research_needed: Cache hit rate and refetch waste vs size and policy (FIFO/LRU/ARC, adjacent-merge) on realistic multi-entry traces, warm and cold.

requirement_or_question: Before decoding, payload ranges for the whole closure are prefetched; neighbours are merged only when purposes are identical (Chunk vs Lookback never merge), the gap is within coalesce_gap_bytes and the merged range stays within max_individual_range_bytes; coalescing changes only request shape: verification and output are identical with coalescing disabled.
research_needed: Differential coalesced/uncoalesced sessions over corpora and HTTP; hostile-gap amplification tests.

requirement_or_question: Default coalescing gap (4096 bytes), range and aggregate limits and the same-diagnostic-purpose restriction are neither specified in docs nor justified by measurement; naive content-addressed HTTP designs pay one request per changed object (OSTree static deltas), so request shaping matters.
research_needed: Request-count/bytes/latency trade-offs of gap thresholds and cross-purpose merging across RTTs, chunk sizes and many-small-entry reads (physical order locality: see prefetch-hot-set-ordering).
decision_needed: What are the default coalescing parameters, and should cross-purpose ranges coalesce?

requirement_or_question: HttpRangeSource accepts only http/https, disables transparent decompression, sends HEAD with identity encoding and requires success, exactly one Content-Length, Accept-Ranges: bytes, a strong quoted ETag (weak W/ refused) and identity encoding; each GET sends Range, If-Match initial ETag and identity encoding; responses must be 206 with the same ETag, exact Content-Length, literal Content-Range and exact body length (412 is SourceUnstable); 200 is never accepted as whole-body fallback.

requirement_or_question: The HTTP source is a blocking client with serial range fetching: no authentication or custom headers, proxy or custom CA configuration, explicit timeouts, retries/backoff for transient errors, multi-range requests, parallel connections or HTTP/2 multiplexing, and no stated redaction of credential-bearing URLs in reports and traces.
